title: Exceptions
learningGoals: catch it with try and catch

youtube.title: C++ Exceptions: try, catch and throw | C++ Programming EP 82
youtube.description: In this episode you will throw an exception, catch it with try and catch and order catch blocks correctly, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Exceptions · 0:45 Throw and catch · 1:26 The path of an exception · 1:56 Second program · 2:56 Recap · 3:26 Bug of the Day · 4:14 Challenge · 4:34 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "TRY / CATCH" in tomato on cream; Xecxec next to a crab catching a falling red ball with a net; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a crab catching a falling red ball with a net

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we handle errors without crashing. We throw an exception, and we catch it where we know what to do.

scenes.onScreen: "Exceptions": numbered lines (1. Throw raises an error; 2. Catch handles it; 3. Put the specific catch first) and an analogy card: a ball thrown up the stairs until someone catches it
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: When code cannot go on, it throws an exception. The program leaves the current function, and looks up the stack for a matching catch block. Think of a ball thrown up the stairs. It goes up until someone catches it. If nobody catches it, the program stops.

analogy.title: Exceptions
analogy.body: A ball thrown up the stairs until someone catches it

scenes.onScreen: throw.cpp: divide throws, and main catches
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 6] The function checks for a bad input. [HL 7] Throw raises a runtime error with a message. [HL 13] Main puts the risky calls inside a try block. [HL 14] The first call works, and prints four. [HL 15] The second call throws. The program jumps out of the try block. The line after it never runs. [HL 17] The catch block receives the exception by const reference. [HL 18] What returns the message. [HL 20] After the catch, the program goes on.

code.output:
4
error: cannot divide by zero
done

scenes.animation: Steps drop in left to right with a pop; connecting arrows draw on; the active step glows butter
scenes.narration: The exception leaves divide at once. This is called unwinding. The program looks for a matching catch in main. When it finds one, the program goes on after the catch block.

scenes.onScreen: catchorder.cpp: two catch blocks, the specific one first
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 8] Stoi cannot read a number from this text, so it throws invalid argument. [HL 10] The first catch is specific, so it matches. [HL 11] It prints bad number. [HL 12] The general catch comes last. It catches every other standard error. Always put the specific catch first.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as catchorder dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints bad number.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. Throw raises an exception. Two. Catch handles it. Three. The program unwinds until a catch matches. Four. Put specific catch blocks before general ones. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: The program unwinds until a catch matches.
Put specific catch blocks before general ones.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: An exception nobody catches
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; the program crashes and the run-time error appears in tomato; the fix slides in and the output turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We throw, and nobody catches. The program ends with terminate called after throwing. Add a try block and a catch block.

scenes.onScreen: Why did the exception get a medal? It was thrown, and someone finally caught it.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: Why did the exception get a medal? It was thrown, and someone finally caught it.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: catch an out of range index
scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Call at with a bad index on a vector. Catch the out of range exception, and print a friendly message. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.onScreen: Next: EP 83 · File input and output
scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: file input and output. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

challenge: Call at with a bad index on a vector. Catch the out of range exception, and print a friendly message.
challengeAnswer: Put the at call in a try block. Catch const out of range reference, and print your own message.
